correctness.rationale: The exact seven-term norm calculation yields signed gap 2(A(p)-8)/3, with A(p)=3||[1,1]||p+||[3,4]||p strictly decreasing, A(3)>8>A(4), and A(∞)=7. For real n=3 the classical sign triple gives 4*3^(1/p)-6<0 because p>q>3>p0, and zero padding extends both witnesses. Real normed planes have the HH property by planar-zonoid support-function representation, and one complex coordinate is Hilbertian. The phase-optimization equality condition follows from Cauchy–Schwarz, independent of p. Endpoints and normalization were independently recomputed. CHECK.py reconstructs actual seven norms on representative exponents and verifies the exact expression but is only supplementary.

value.rationale: Identifies the minimum number of scalar coordinates required for HH failure as exactly two over C versus three over R throughout an explicit open exponent interval, the first dimension in which scalar-field choice matters for this family. The 3–4–5 phase yields transparent exact scalar norms and an intrinsic phase-optimality lemma. This is a motivated geometric boundary across a full family, not a numerical isolated example. The theorem explicitly avoids unsupported assertions of a global optimal exponent.
